messages:
Irene: Heads up — seeing a sudden burst of 502s from edge for hosted-api /v1/embeddings (batching path) starting ~09:09 UTC. Started right after the tenant-hash rollout at 09:07. Any ideas?
Ava: saw that too, 502 rate jumped to ~7-9% for a couple tenants. Spike aligns with the rollout.
Raj: digging into Envoy traces — a lot of 'upstream connect error' and 'no healthy upstream' for a subset of tenant shards. Example trace-id: tx-8f3a9. Pasting envoy snippets: ```envoy error: cluster "tenant-shard-17" no healthy upstream
[2024-03-07T09:09:22Z] src/proxy.cc: upstream connect error: connection reset by peer
```
infra-bot: deploy-bot: rollout tenant-hash-lowercase v3 started at 1709812021, batch=canary, status=success for canary group.
Irene: quick repro: ```curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Tenant-ID: T42" -X POST https://api.hosted.redwood/v1/embeddings -d @sample.json``` returns 502 with body "{\"error\":\"proxy_error\"}" for T42 but works for some other tenants.
Ava: hypothesis — new hash function normalizes header case; some frontdoor/edge proxies still emit mixed-case X-Tenant-ID -> sticky routing ended up hitting backends that were cold or missing model mounts (warmup race). Those backends then rejected streams and Envoy returned 502.
Raj: found backend logs on host node-7: ```ERROR model_loader: mount failed for tenant_T42: volume not mounted
ERROR runtime: start_stream(): upstream rejected connection
``` Also see tenant routing header in access logs: `X-Tenant-Id: T42` vs `x-tenant-id: t42` in different hops.
Irene: can we pause/rollback the hash change? If routing keys became inconsistent, we should revert until we make header normalization backwards compatible.
oncall: rollback initiated for tenant-hash-lowercase v3 -> v2 at 1709812360. Pausing further rollout. Will watch 502 rate.
Ava: mitigation notes: 1) rollback 2) add header-normalization shim at frontdoor to canonicalize tenant header case 3) add probe to detect model mount health before marking upstream healthy. 4) add small warmup window for new nodes receiving sticky traffic.
Raj: after rollback 502s dropped back to baseline (~0.2%) within ~45s for affected tenants. I'll file an infra follow-up with logs and a small reproducer. Trace examples attached in thread (tx-8f3a9, tx-9b4c2).
Irene: thx all — cataloging steps for support ticket and customers that reported increased 502s. Will add customer-facing note linking to incident update. :white_check_mark:
